title: Whole Numbers to 9 Digits: Place Value, Comparing and Ordering
seo_title: Grade 6 Whole Numbers to 9 Digits Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Count forwards and backwards in whole number intervals and fractions; order, compare and represent numbers to at least 9-digit numbers; represent odd and even numbers to at least 1 000 000; recognise the place value of digits in whole numbers to at least 9-digit numbers.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 6 whole numbers worksheets: 9-digit place value, reading and writing numbers, expanded notation, comparing and ordering. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Millions, thousands, units: three groups of three digits.
key_sub: Count the digits first, then compare from the left.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A 9-digit number has three groups: millions, thousands and units: 345 208 917.
  • In 345 208 917 the 4 is worth 40 000 000 (forty million).
  • Write 0 for an empty place: three million and five = 3 000 005.
  • To compare, count the digits first. With the same number of digits, compare from the left.

Examples

Example

Twelve million four hundred and six thousand and thirty

12 million

406 thousand

030

Answer: 12 406 030

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Value or digit?The digit 4 in 345 208 917 has a value of 40 000 000.
A missing 0Write 0 for every empty place.
Fewer digits, bigger numberCount the digits first.

faq.a: With a space between groups of three digits: 345 208 917.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 8 is in the hundred thousands place, so it is worth 8 hundred thousands = 800 000. The digit is 8, but its value is 800 000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 3 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 3 thousands = 3 000. The digit is 3, but its value is 3 000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 2 is in the millions place, so it is worth 2 million = 2 000 000. The digit is 2, but its value is 2 000 000.

items.q: In 7 568 219, which digit is in the hundred thousands place?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands, millions. In 7 568 219 the hundred thousands digit is 5, worth 500 000.

items.q: In 3 427 085, which digit is in the ten thousands place?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands, millions. In 3 427 085 the ten thousands digit is 2, worth 20 000.

items.q: Which number has a 5 in the hundred thousands place?
items.e: The hundred thousands place is the 6th digit from the right (the first digit after the millions). In 2 538 971 the 5 is there, so it is worth 500 000.

items.q: What number is 600 000 + 5 000 + 30?
items.e: Put each digit in its place and write 0 in every empty place: 600 000 + 5 000 + 30 = 605 030.

items.q: Which number is four hundred six thousand five?
items.e: Write each group as three digits. Four hundred six thousand → 406. Then five → 005. Fill every empty place with 0: 406 005.

items.q: At the 2 021 census, British Columbia had five million eight hundred seventy-nine people. Which number is this?
items.e: Write each group as three digits. Five million → 5. No thousands → 000. Eight hundred seventy-nine → 879. So 5 | 000 | 879 = 5 000 879. The empty thousands group still needs three zeros.

items.q: How do you read 1 000 000 000?
items.e: 1 000 000 000 has four groups: 1 | 000 | 000 | 000. The fourth group from the right is billions, so it is one billion.

items.q: Which number is twelve million five thousand?
items.e: Twelve million → 12. Five thousand → 005 in the thousands group. No ones → 000. So 12 | 005 | 000 = 12 005 000.

items.q: How do you read 4 050 300 000?
c: four billion five hundred million three hundred thousand
four million fifty thousand three hundred
four billion fifty million three hundred thousand
four billion fifty million three thousand
items.e: Groups: 4 | 050 | 300 | 000. That is 4 billion, 50 million and 300 thousand: four billion fifty million three hundred thousand.

items.q: Write 4 300 000 as a number of millions.
Karabo has the digit cards 7, 0, 3, 9, 1, 5 and 2. She uses each card once to make the smallest 7-digit number she can. What number does she make?
items.e: Put the smallest digits first, but a 7-digit number cannot start with 0. Start with 1, then 0, then 2, 3, 5, 7, 9: 1 023 579. (0 123 579 is really 123 579, a 6-digit number.)

items.q: A museum had 1 463 000 visitors in a year. Ofentse rounds this to the nearest 100 000 first, then rounds her answer to the nearest 1 000 000 and gets 2 000 000. What is 1 463 000 rounded to the nearest 1 000 000?
items.e: Always round the original number. Look at the hundred thousands digit of 1 463 000: 4. 4 or less, so round down to 1 000 000. Rounding twice (1 463 000 → 1 500 000 → 2 000 000) gives the wrong answer.

items.q: A theme park had 1 995 800 visitors last year. This year it had 10 000 more. How many visitors did it have this year?
items.e: Add 1 to the ten thousands digit: 9 + 1 = 10, so exchange for 1 hundred thousand. Then 9 + 1 = 10 hundred thousands, so exchange for 1 million. 1 995 800 + 10 000 = 2 005 800.

items.q: A newspaper says “about 60 000 fans” went to a concert. The number was rounded to the nearest 1 000. Which could be the real number of fans?
items.e: Numbers from 59 500 to 60 499 round to 60 000. 59 612 is in that range. 60 512 and 60 500 round up to 61 000, and 59 412 rounds down to 59 000.

items.q: A diver is 12 m below sea level. A seagull is flying 15 m above sea level, straight above the diver. How far apart are they?
items.e: From 12 m below sea level up to sea level is 12 m. From sea level up to the seagull is 15 m. 12 + 15 = 27 m. (15 − 12 = 3 is the mistake of not crossing 0.)

items.q: The population of a town, rounded to the nearest 10 000, is 250 000. What is the smallest the population could be?
items.e: Numbers from 245 000 to 254 999 round to 250 000. 244 999 would round down to 240 000, so the smallest is 245 000. (254 999 is the greatest.)

items.q: A crowd of 74 310 fans watched a cup final. What is the crowd to the nearest 1 000?
items.e: 74 310 is between 74 000 and 75 000. Look at the hundreds digit: 3. 4 or less, so round down. Answer: 74 000 fans.

items.q: A soccer club’s total attendance for the season was two million, forty thousand and fifty. How is this written in digits?
items.e: 2 million → 2, forty thousand → 040, fifty → 050. Fill every empty place with 0: 2 040 050.

items.q: The average distance from the Earth to the Moon is 384 400 km. What is this to the nearest 10 000 km?
items.e: 384 400 is between 380 000 and 390 000. Look at the thousands digit: 4. 4 or less, so round down. Answer: 380 000 km.

items.q: How many zeros does one billion have when you write it in digits?
items.e: One billion = 1 000 000 000: three groups of three zeros, so 9 zeros. One million has 6 zeros.

items.q: How many millions are there in one billion?
items.e: 1 000 000 000 ÷ 1 000 000 = 1 000. Each period is 1 000 times the period before it: 1 000 thousands make a million, and 1 000 millions make a billion.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 4 is in the hundred thousands place, so it is worth 4 hundred thousands = 400 000. The digit is 4, but its value is 400 000.

items.q: In 770 000 000, the first 7 is worth how many times the second 7?
items.e: The first 7 is worth 700 000 000. The second 7 is worth 70 000 000. 700 000 000 ÷ 70 000 000 = 10. Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right.
Put each digit in its place and write 0 in every empty place: 800 000 000 + 6 000 000 + 9 000 + 30 = 806 009 030.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the ten thousands place: 9 ten thousands is more than 8 ten thousands. So 6 098 450 > 6 089 450.

items.q: What is 10 000 more than 4 995 300?
items.e: Add 1 to the ten thousands digit: 9 ten thousands + 1 = 10 ten thousands. Exchange them for 1 hundred thousand, then 9 + 1 = 10 hundred thousands, so exchange again for 1 million. 4 995 300 + 10 000 = 5 005 300.

items.q: What is 100 000 less than 2 034 500?
items.e: There are 0 hundred thousands, so exchange 1 million for 10 hundred thousands. 10 − 1 = 9 hundred thousands and 1 million is left. 2 034 500 − 100 000 = 1 934 500.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the ten thousands place: 7 ten thousands is more than 3 ten thousands. So 1 576 324 > 1 537 624. 1 576 324 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the thousands place: 9 thousands is more than 2 thousands. So 7 359 246 > 7 352 496. 7 352 496 is the smallest.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 2 000 000 to 3 000 000 there are 10 equal jumps, so each mark is 100 000, not 10 000. The arrow is 7 marks after 2 000 000: 2 000 000 + 700 000 = 2 700 000.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 5 000 000 to 6 000 000 there are 10 equal jumps, so each mark is 100 000, not 10 000. The arrow is 4 marks after 5 000 000: 5 000 000 + 400 000 = 5 400 000.

items.q: Put 5 297 184, 5 792 814, 5 298 714 in order from smallest to greatest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 5 297 184 < 5 298 714 (thousands: 7 < 8). 5 298 714 < 5 792 814 (hundred thousands: 2 < 7). So the order is 5 297 184, 5 298 714, 5 792 814.

items.q: Put 6 874 921, 6 784 129, 6 784 291 in order from smallest to greatest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 6 784 129 < 6 784 291 (hundreds: 1 < 2). 6 784 291 < 6 874 921 (hundred thousands: 7 < 8). So the order is 6 784 129, 6 784 291, 6 874 921.

items.q: Put 3 869 527, 3 865 729, 3 895 627 in order from greatest to smallest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 3 865 729 < 3 869 527 (thousands: 5 < 9). 3 869 527 < 3 895 627 (ten thousands: 6 < 9). So the order is 3 895 627, 3 869 527, 3 865 729.

items.q: What is 10 000 more than 495 300?
items.e: Add 1 to the ten thousands digit: 9 ten thousands + 1 = 10 ten thousands. Regroup them as 1 hundred thousand: 4 + 1 = 5 hundred thousands. 495 300 + 10 000 = 505 300.

items.q: What is 10 000 less than 203 450?
items.e: There are 0 ten thousands, so regroup 1 hundred thousand as 10 ten thousands. 10 − 1 = 9 ten thousands and 1 hundred thousand is left. 203 450 − 10 000 = 193 450.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the thousands place: 5 thousands is more than 3 thousands. So 675 391 > 673 951. 673 951 is the least.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 300 000 to 400 000 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 10 000, not 1 000. The arrow is 7 spaces after 300 000: 300 000 + 70 000 = 370 000.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 0 to 1 000 000 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 100 000. The arrow is 1 space after 500 000: 500 000 + 100 000 = 600 000.

items.q: Put 423 618, 462 318, 436 218 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 423 618 < 436 218 (ten thousands: 2 < 3). 436 218 < 462 318 (ten thousands: 3 < 6). So the order is 423 618, 436 218, 462 318.

items.q: Put 471 683, 468 713, 476 813 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 468 713 < 471 683 (ten thousands: 6 < 7). 471 683 < 476 813 (thousands: 1 < 6). So the order is 468 713, 471 683, 476 813.

items.q: Put 831 672, 867 312, 861 273 in order from greatest to least.
items.e: Compare from the left. 831 672 < 861 273 (ten thousands: 3 < 6). 861 273 < 867 312 (thousands: 1 < 7). So the order is 867 312, 861 273, 831 672.

items.q: 52☐ 400 > 527 600. Which digit could go in the box?
items.e: The hundred thousands and ten thousands are the same. Compare the thousands: the box must be 7 or more. If it is 7, compare the hundreds: 4 < 6, so 527 400 is too small. 528 400 > 527 600.

items.q: 3☐4 500 < 312 900. Which digit could go in the box?
items.e: The hundred thousands are the same. Compare the ten thousands: the box must be 1 or less. If it is 1, compare the thousands: 4 > 2, so 314 500 is too big. 304 500 < 312 900.

items.q: Which is greater: 2 billion or 900 million?
items.e: 2 billion = 2 000 000 000 (10 digits). 900 million = 900 000 000 (9 digits). A billion is 1 000 millions, so 2 billion is much greater, even though 900 > 2.

items.q: Compare 0,45 and 0,5.
items.e: 0,5 = 0,50. Compare the tenths: 4 tenths < 5 tenths. So 0,45 < 0,5. More digits does not mean a greater number.

items.q: Compare 0,7 and 0,69.
items.e: 0,7 = 0,70. Compare the tenths: 7 > 6. So 0,7 > 0,69.

items.q: Compare 5,06 and 5,060.
items.e: A 0 at the end does not change the value. 5,06 = 5,060.

items.q: Compare 0,004 and 0,04.
items.e: 0,04 = 0,040. Compare the hundredths: 0 < 4. So 0,004 < 0,04. 4 thousandths is less than 4 hundredths.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: All have 7 digits. Millions, hundred thousands and ten thousands are the same in 5 000 879 and 5 000 978, and both have 0 thousands. Compare the hundreds: 8 < 9. 5 008 790 and 5 080 790 have more thousands. So 5 000 879 is the least.

items.q: Compare 0,215 and 0,22.
items.e: Write both with 3 places: 0,215 and 0,220. The tenths are the same. Compare the hundredths: 1 < 2. So 0,215 < 0,22. Do not compare 215 with 22.

items.q: Compare 3,9 and 3,899.
items.e: 3,9 = 3,900. The ones are the same. Compare the tenths: 9 > 8. So 3,9 > 3,899.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 0,800; 0,790; 0,799; 0,087. Compare the tenths first: only 0,8 has 8 tenths. So 0,8 is the greatest.

items.q: Order from least to greatest: 0,5; 0,45; 0,405
items.e: Write them with 3 places: 0,500; 0,450; 0,405. Compare 500, 450 and 405 thousandths. So 0,405; 0,45; 0,5.

items.q: In 968 340, which digit is in the ten thousands place?

items.q: In 821 974, which digit is in the thousands place?

items.q: Which number is two hundred thirty thousand seven hundred eight?
items.e: Write each group as three digits. Two hundred thirty thousand → 230. Then seven hundred eight → 708. Fill every empty place with 0: 230 708.

items.q: Which number is nine hundred thousand four hundred thirty?
items.e: Write each group as three digits. Nine hundred thousand → 900. Then four hundred thirty → 430. Fill every empty place with 0: 900 430.

items.q: How many thousands are there in one million?
items.e: 1 000 000 ÷ 1 000 = 1 000. Ten hundred thousands make one million, and each hundred thousand is 100 thousands: 10 × 100 = 1 000 thousands.
